question: The Gopurams of the Chidambaram temple contain many poses of which dance form?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatnatyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Chidambaram temple, also known as Thillai Nataraja Temple, is dedicated to Lord Shiva in his form of Nataraja, the cosmic dancer.
 
• Bharatnatyam is a classical Indian dance form originating from Tamil Nadu, which is known for its fixed upper torso, bent legs, and intricate footwork combined with expressive hand gestures and facial expressions.
 
• The Gopurams of the Chidambaram temple are famous for their artistic and intricate architecture, which includes many sculptures depicting the various poses of Bharatnatyam.
 
• Bharatnatyam is one of the oldest classical dance traditions in India, and it has been an essential part of Tamil culture and heritage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chidambaram Temple**

 
 
• The Chidambaram Temple is located in the town of Chidambaram in Tamil Nadu, India.
 
• It is one of the most ancient and celebrated shrines in India, dating back to the Chola dynasty.
 
• The temple is renowned for its magnificent architecture, including its four Gopurams (gateway towers), which are covered with sculptures depicting various mythological stories and dance forms.
 
• The temple is particularly famous for its association with Lord Shiva as Nataraja, the lord of dance, and it is a significant pilgrimage site for devotees of Shiva.
 
 
 
• **Bharatnatyam**
 
 
• Bharatnatyam is a major classical dance form that originated in Tamil Nadu, India.
 
• It is known for its grace, purity, tenderness, and sculpturesque poses.
 
• The dance form has its roots in the Natya Shastra, an ancient Indian treatise on dance and drama written by Bharata Muni.
 
• Traditionally, Bharatnatyam was performed by Devadasis (temple dancers) in the temples of Tamil Nadu as a form of worship.
 
• Today, it is performed on stage and has gained international recognition as one of the classical dance forms of India.
